title: A DC motor's current falls as its back EMF grows
caption: The 2 Ω motor on 24 V draws I = (24 − ε_b)/2. At the start there is no back EMF, so I = 12 A, four times the running current. As it speeds up ε_b rises, until at full speed it is 18 V and the current is 3 A: 24 − 3 × 2 = 18 V.
alt: Graph of motor current against back EMF: a straight line falling from 12 A at 0 V to 3 A at 18 V.
description: The horizontal axis is the back EMF in volts; the vertical axis is the motor current in amperes.
With V = 24 V and R = 2 Ω, I = (24 − ε_b)/2: 12 A when ε_b = 0 (switch-on).
At full speed I = 3 A, so ε_b = 24 − 3 × 2 = 18 V.
